Latest Travel stories

Travel

Sat Nov 7aviation

FAA says first U.S. digital air traffic control towers are live in Florida and Alaska

The Federal Aviation Administration said the nation's first digital air traffic control towers are operational at Bartow Executive Airport in Florida and Kenai Municipal Airport in Alaska.

Fri Nov 6aviation

Hoax bomb threats disrupt dozens of flights across Europe

Hoax bomb threats disrupted dozens of flights across Europe on Thursday, with The Guardian reporting at least 25 threats that day and AFP saying about 20 commercial flights were hit; no explosives were found.

Fri Nov 6aviation

FAA to replace floppy-disk ATC displays with E-IDS at 435 sites by 2028

The Federal Aviation Administration said on Thursday it will replace decades-old floppy-disk systems that carry weather and other critical information with the Enterprise Information Display System, planning installations at 435 sites by the end of 2028.

Fri Nov 6aviation

Argentine state workers' union postpones airport protests for Pope Leo visit

Argentina's Asociación Trabajadores del Estado (ATE) on Thursday temporarily suspended protests planned for Friday at more than 27 airports after the country's Episcopal Conference asked it not to disrupt Pope Leo XIV's upcoming visit.

Thu Nov 5rail

French national strike cancels one in 10 TGV trains and three Eurostar services

A nationwide strike in France over wages on Thursday led SNCF to cancel about one in 10 high-speed TGV trains and disrupt regional and Paris-area services, while Eurostar cancelled trains 9004, 9015 and 9052, according to SNCF forecasts reported by BFM Business and Eurostar's travel updates.

Thu Nov 5aviation

JetBlue raises checked bag fees for the second time this year, to at least $50

JetBlue raised its checked bag fees for bookings made on or after November 3, with the first checked bag now costing at least $50 one way, The Washington Post reported.

Thu Nov 5aviation

FAA proposes inspecting overhead bins on 1,370 U.S. Airbus A320-family jets

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposed on Thursday a one-time inspection of overhead bins made by supplier ARIES on Airbus A318, A319, A320 and A321 planes, after parts at the bins' attachment points were found to have moved out of position, according to the Federal Register.

Mon Nov 2aviation

Global passenger-processing outage knocks out self check-in at Singapore's Changi Airport

A global disruption in Advance Passenger Processing systems shut down some self-service check-in kiosks at all four terminals of Singapore's Changi Airport on Monday morning local time, airport operator Changi Airport Group said.

Mon Nov 2aviation

Naples airport closes for all of November for runway rebuild, shifting some flights to Salerno

Naples International Airport is closed to air traffic from November 1 to 30 while its runway and taxiways are rebuilt, operator GESAC said, with some flights moved to Salerno Costa d'Amalfi Airport.

Fri Oct 30regulation

Airline groups push back as CDC requires every US-bound air traveler to sign an Ebola attestation

Starting at 11:59 p.m. EST on November 3, everyone flying to the United States from abroad, including crew, must sign a paper or digital attestation that they have not been in the Democratic Republic of Congo in the past 21 days, under an amended CDC order published Friday.

Fri Oct 30aviation

ANA Holdings plans to take full control of Japanese regional airlines Airdo and Solaseed Air

ANA Holdings said on Thursday it plans to make RegionalPlus Wings, the holding company of Airdo and Solaseed Air, a wholly owned subsidiary through a share swap taking effect in April 2027.

Thu Oct 29travel

Frontier's average fare jumps 71% as the budget airline posts record revenue but a quarterly loss

Frontier Airlines said third-quarter revenue rose 53% to a record $1.4B, while fare revenue per passenger climbed to $67.82 from $39.74 a year earlier, according to the company and CNBC.

Thu Oct 29travel

Alaska Airlines plans daily Anchorage-Tokyo Narita nonstop flights from May 2027

Alaska Airlines said it plans to fly daily between Anchorage and Tokyo Narita from May 13 to September 7, 2027, subject to government approval, according to the airline and Aviation Week.

Wed Oct 28travel

Residential cruise ship Villa Vie Odyssey halts its world voyage in Cambodia, citing fuel costs

Villa Vie Residences has suspended operations of the MV Odyssey in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, saying monthly fuel costs per cabin have jumped from about $1,800 to an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia.

Wed Oct 28aviation

Norwegian beats profit forecasts but trims early 2027 capacity on fuel costs

Norwegian Air Shuttle reported third-quarter operating profit of NOK 2.7B, above the NOK 2.3B analysts expected, Reuters reported, while cutting planned first-quarter 2027 capacity by more than 5%.

Tue Oct 27immigration

US suspends visa-free travel program for Chinese visitors to the Northern Mariana Islands

The Department of Homeland Security is suspending EVS-TAP, which lets pre-screened Chinese nationals visit the Northern Mariana Islands without a visa, effective 2 p.m. EDT on October 30, according to a Federal Register notice.

Tue Oct 27aviation

JetBlue posts wider third-quarter loss as fuel costs jump 57%

JetBlue reported a third-quarter net loss of $257M, up from $143M a year earlier, as its average fuel price rose 57% to $3.91 a gallon, even as revenue grew 21.1% to $2.8B.

Mon Oct 26aviation

Houthi attacks have canceled 86% of Riyadh flights this month as airport partly reopens

About 4,071 of 4,736 scheduled flights at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport were canceled from Oct. 8 to Oct. 25, Reuters reported, citing Cirium data, as Saudi authorities partly reopened the airport on Sunday.

Mon Oct 26aviation

IndiGo and Air India to move some Mumbai flights to new Navi Mumbai airport

The airlines will shift selected flights from Mumbai's main airport to Navi Mumbai International Airport starting in December, freeing space to rebuild the older airport's Terminal 1.

Sun Oct 25aviation

Western Sydney International Airport opens to passengers

Sydney's new A$5.6 billion airport opened to passengers on Sunday, the first major new airport in Australia in more than 50 years, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said.

Fri Oct 23aviation

American Airlines forecasts deeper 2026 loss as fuel costs soar

American now expects an adjusted full-year loss of $1.00 to $1.60 a share and plans to slow growth in 2027, as US carriers lean on higher fares to offset jet fuel costs.

Fri Oct 23aviation

Drone attacks shut all four Moscow airports for second time in two days

Russia's aviation agency halted flights at Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, Vnukovo and Zhukovsky on Friday afternoon as air defenses engaged drones approaching the capital.

Fri Oct 23regulation

FAA releases draft design standards for vertiports and heliports

The FAA proposed combined design standards for facilities serving helicopters, air taxis and other vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, with final standards expected in summer 2027.

modals.2026-10-23-travel-1:
Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Travel Digest · aviation

American Airlines forecasts deeper 2026 loss as fuel costs soar

American reported record third-quarter revenue of $16.3 billion, up 19.3%, but posted a net loss of $269 million as fuel expense jumped 67.5%. It expects to pay about $4.70 a gallon in the fourth quarter, nearly double a year earlier, and said network growth will slow in 2027. CEO Robert Isom said he expects the airline to return to profit next year.

American is the fourth major US airline to cut its 2026 outlook this month because of fuel, after Delta, United and Southwest, CNBC reported. Reuters reported that carriers are favoring higher fares over fuller planes, and CNBC cited airline reports and federal data showing fares up more than 20% from last year.

Why it matters: Airlines are protecting margins by holding back capacity and raising prices, so travelers are paying more heading into the holiday season.

modals.2026-10-23-travel-2:
Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Travel Digest · aviation

Drone attacks shut all four Moscow airports for second time in two days

Rosaviatsiya restricted all four airports at about 14:05 Moscow time, citing flight safety. Sheremetyevo declared an air-raid alert and moved passengers, including some from parked aircraft, into shelters. Vnukovo and Domodedovo resumed flights under a clearance regime by 16:43, while restrictions at Sheremetyevo and Zhukovsky were still in place at that time, AeroTime reported, citing agency notices.

It was the second full closure in two days, after an overnight shutdown on Oct. 22. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said air defenses destroyed drones flying toward the city; those claims could not be independently verified.

Why it matters: Repeated closures cause delays, cancellations and diversions for travelers, including on foreign carriers that still fly to Moscow, such as Emirates.

    AeroTime · aerotime.aero · 2026-10-23
  2. Ukrainian drone attack triggers shut down of Moscow airports

modals.2026-10-23-travel-3:
Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Travel Digest · regulation

FAA releases draft design standards for vertiports and heliports

The draft covers touchdown and liftoff areas, approach surfaces, lighting and markings, fueling and electric charging, rooftop and elevated landing sites, and how to add vertical-flight facilities at existing airports without disrupting current operations. It combines the FAA's earlier separate guidance for heliports and vertiports.

The agency called the draft an initial proposal for industry feedback and said it will seek public comment before publishing final standards in summer 2027. Data from its eVTOL Integration Pilot Program will help refine future standards, the FAA said.

Why it matters: Companies developing electric air taxis need approved designs for landing and charging sites before passenger service can grow, and airport and heliport owners will use the standards to plan them.

References

  1. FAA Releases Draft Design Standards for Vertical Flight Facilities
    FAA · faa.gov · 2026-10-23
modals.2026-10-25-wk-10:
Sunday · Oct 25, 2026 · Weekend Digest · aviation

Western Sydney International Airport opens to passengers

A Jetstar flight left the curfew-free airport for the Gold Coast just before 11:30 a.m. Sunday, ABC News Australia reported. The first international flight, bound for New Zealand, is scheduled for Monday morning.

The airport at Badgerys Creek, about 60 km west of central Sydney, will operate 24 hours a day, while the city's current airport can host take-offs and landings only after 6 a.m. and until 11 p.m., Reuters reported via The Straits Times.

Why it matters: Round-the-clock operations give airlines more scheduling options in Australia's most populous city.

modals.2026-10-26-travel-1:
Monday · Oct 26, 2026 · Travel Digest · aviation

Houthi attacks have canceled 86% of Riyadh flights this month as airport partly reopens

Domestic flights resumed from Terminal 1 and Saudi national carriers were allowed to fly international services from Terminal 2, Reuters reported. The Houthis said they attacked the airport again on Monday; Saudi Arabia said air defenses intercepted a ballistic missile fired toward Riyadh, CNA reported. Across the kingdom, more than 7,800 flights, or 45% of scheduled departures, were canceled between Oct. 8 and Oct. 25, according to Cirium.

International airlines have suspended Riyadh service into November, and Delta Air Lines has postponed the launch of its Riyadh route until next year, Reuters reported. The US Embassy said Jeddah and Dammam airports are operating with some delays and cancellations, and that land border crossings, including the King Fahd Causeway to Bahrain, remain open.

Why it matters: Travelers to Saudi Arabia face continuing cancellations. The State Department ordered non-emergency US government staff and their families to leave the country effective Oct. 23.

modals.2026-10-26-travel-2:
Monday · Oct 26, 2026 · Travel Digest · aviation

IndiGo and Air India to move some Mumbai flights to new Navi Mumbai airport

Air India Express will start four daily domestic flights from Navi Mumbai in December 2026 and move its Oman services there from January 2027, followed by flights to Jeddah, Riyadh, Dammam, Doha, Muscat and Sharjah by the Northern Summer 2027 season, Air India said. IndiGo will move 12 daily international departures, including all its current Mumbai flights to Bahrain, Riyadh, Jeddah, Kuwait, Muscat, Dhaka and Jakarta, between February and July 2027, according to a joint statement with the airport operator reported by The Hindu.

The airlines and the airport operator said carriers will keep their historical slots at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport. The first phase aims to move about 5 million passengers; the existing airport handles around 55 million a year.

Why it matters: Travelers flying through Mumbai will need to check which of the city's two airports their flight uses as the shift rolls out.

modals.2026-10-27-travel-1:
Tuesday · Oct 27, 2026 · Travel Digest · immigration

US suspends visa-free travel program for Chinese visitors to the Northern Mariana Islands

The suspension covers new applicants and existing travel authorizations. Chinese nationals already in the CNMI under the program may stay for their authorized period but will need a visa for future trips. The program, in place since February 2025, allowed stays of up to 14 days in the CNMI only, and more than 3,000 Chinese nationals used it in fiscal 2025, DHS said.

DHS cited security risks including possible espionage near military sites in the region, smuggling of travelers onward to Guam, and birth tourism. CNMI Delegate Kimberlyn King-Hinds said the program was "suspended, not terminated" and warned that a long disruption would hurt the islands' tourism industry, Public Radio Guam reported.

Why it matters: Tourism is central to the CNMI economy, and Chinese visitors will now need to go through the standard US visa process.

References

  1. Suspension of the CNMI Economic Vitality & Security Travel Authorization Program (EVS-TAP)
    Federal Register (DHS) · federalregister.gov · 2026-10-27
  2. CNMI delegate urges path forward as DHS halts Chinese travel program

modals.2026-10-27-travel-2:
Tuesday · Oct 27, 2026 · Travel Digest · aviation

JetBlue posts wider third-quarter loss as fuel costs jump 57%

The carrier ended the quarter with $2.2B in liquidity, including a $600M undrawn credit facility, and said its unencumbered assets had grown to about $7B, including $2.8B in aircraft and engines. It now expects full-year unit revenue to rise 13.5% to 14.5%.

JetBlue shares rose more than 12% in early trading on Tuesday after the update, Reuters reported. Fuel costs have climbed since the war with Iran began, and JetBlue had lost roughly 48% of its share value, making it the worst-performing US carrier, according to Reuters.

Why it matters: Airlines have leaned on higher fares to offset fuel costs, and JetBlue's results show how much of the increase it has been able to pass on.

References

  1. JetBlue Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results
    JetBlue · nasdaq.com · 2026-10-27
  2. JetBlue shares rally as airline seeks to calm financial concerns
    Reuters (via Investing.com) · investing.com · 2026-10-27
modals.2026-10-28-travel-1:
Wednesday · Oct 28, 2026 · Travel Digest · travel

Residential cruise ship Villa Vie Odyssey halts its world voyage in Cambodia, citing fuel costs

The ship was carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, and 156 crew, according to Cambodian officials cited by AP. The Florida-based operator said it is helping residents leave the ship and find temporary housing, though one passenger wrote online that the company had not helped them find hotels, AP reported. A provincial official said the ship was expected to refuel and leave Cambodia on Saturday, but the operator has not confirmed a date.
